validity.recommendation: No action required. Real, correctly-classified, correctly-attributed asset; only the caveats below (spec history, minor state-coverage gap) are worth a future researcher's attention.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently of GEM/gem.wiki. This is PNGRB's (Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board) authorized 'KG Basin Network' -- entry #7 in the current (May 2026) line-wise Operational Common Carrier Pipeline table, authorised 12.05.2010, and it appears under the SAME name/entity/date in the Jan-2016 and Feb-2024 editions of the same register (three separate dated publications spanning a decade, not one document copy-pasted -- the length figure itself changed between editions, proving each edition is independently re-derived, see spec caveat below). Existence and real-world operation are further corroborated by two genuinely independent, non-PNGRB sources: (1) Business Standard financial news (18 Mar 2016), reporting that PNGRB raised the tariff on 'the company's [GAIL's] K.G. Basin natural gas pipeline network' effective 1 Apr 2016 -- a live regulatory/commercial event that could not exist for a non-existent pipeline; and (2) Times of India's 2014 Nagaram-blast coverage, an independent news investigation confirming a real, physically operating GAIL gas pipeline in East Godavari district, Andhra Pradesh (the same asset -- GAIL has only one gas pipeline system in that district) leaked and exploded, killing 29 people, with a follow-up PNGRB penalty order. This is not a GEM-only or gem.wiki-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is correct. PNGRB authorises this asset as a 'common carrier pipeline network' under Regulation 17(1) of the PNGRB (Authorizing Entities...) Regulations 2008 -- common-carrier transmission-class infrastructure, not a city-gas distribution (CGD) network -- consistent with how GEM treats the sheet's other GAIL 'Regional Network' rows (Assam P0906, Gujarat P0923, Mumbai P0943, Cauvery P0911). DUPLICATE CHECK vs the 35-pipeline India-gas roster: none. The nearest thing geographically is P0938 (Mallavaram-Bhopal-Bhilwara-Vijaipur), which originates at Kunchanapalli near the same KG-basin gas hub -- but that is a long-haul GAIL/GREP trunk line carrying KG-basin (chiefly RIL D6) gas onward to central India (365 km, 78.25 MMSCMD, ends in Telangana), a physically and functionally distinct system from P0933's own local common-carrier network within East Godavari/West Godavari/Krishna districts. No overlap or double-count. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=GAIL (India) Ltd 100% is independently confirmed by PNGRB (sole listed entity across all three register editions) AND by Business Standard ('the company's K.G. Basin...pipeline network', referring to GAIL) -- two independent origins, tier high. Fuel=Gas and the FuelSource attribution are addressed in the fills below.

validity.recommendation: No sheet change. Flagging so a future researcher who finds the original 2010 PNGRB order does not mistake its provisional figures (834.81 km / 4.0 MMSCMD common-carrier capacity) for an error in the current sheet values (877.86 km / 16.00 MMSCMD).
validity.researcher_notes: I pulled and OCR'd the actual primary source cited on gem.wiki for this row's Start/Length/Capacity citations -- PNGRB's original authorization letter, No.Infra/PL/Exis/17/KG-REG/GAIL/01/10 dated 12 May 2010 (a scanned/image PDF with no extractable text layer; pdftotext returns 0 lines, so I ran pdftoppm + tesseract on all 4 pages). That letter states verbatim: 'the said pipeline project which has already been completed and commissioned between year 1991 to 2005' -- this directly and explicitly supports StartYear1=1991 as the start of that range; it is a primary regulatory finding of fact (based on GAIL's submitted proof), not a guess or an authorisation-date mix-up. HOWEVER the same 2010 letter also states: 'The capacity of K.G. Basin Natural Gas Pipeline network, length 834.81 kms, diameter ranging from 2 inches to 18 inches, is equal to 15.997 MMSCMD as indicated by GAIL... The common carrier capacity would thus be 4.0 MMSCMD*' (footnoted as provisional, pending final capacity determination). So at the moment of authorisation (2010) the network was 834.81 km / ~16 MMSCMD total capacity but only 4.0 MMSCMD DECLARED COMMON-CARRIER capacity. Every later PNGRB register edition I could check -- Jan 2016 ('877.9 km, 16.000 MMSCMD'), Feb 2024 ('877.86 km, 16.00 MMSCMD authorised, 19.4 MMSCMD design/determined, 864.90 km operating'), and May 2026 ('878 km authorised, 16.0 MMSCMD authorised / 19.4 MMSCMD design, 867 km operating') -- instead shows an AUTHORISED CAPACITY of ~16 MMSCMD (matching GAIL's originally-indicated total network capacity, not the 4.0 MMSCMD provisional common-carrier figure) and a LENGTH that grew from 834.81 km to 877.86-878 km sometime between 2010 and Jan 2016. I could not locate the specific intermediate order that finalised the higher capacity determination or authorised the extra ~43 km (candidate mechanisms: the 2010 letter's own final-capacity-determination clause, or subsequent GAIL applications not captured in these three summary tables), so I am not proposing a value change -- GEM's current 877.86 km / 16.00 MMSCMD is the value used consistently by the regulator for the last decade (2016-2026), while the 2010 figures are a superseded historical baseline. Treating this as a caveat, not a live disagreement, per the instruction to note material history rather than silently pass it.

I did not find any other source specifying which part of the network reaches Puducherry (it is a small, likely peripheral extension of the East/West Godavari/Krishna-district grid), so I'm not confident enough in a specific location to force a StartLocation/District fill (this is a multi-segment 2-18-inch-diameter local network, not a simple point-to-point line, matching the pattern of other GEM 'Regional Network' rows that also leave Start/End district fields blank). Flagging the Puducherry gap as a completeness caveat rather than proposing an unverified location value.

Confirmed by pdftotext -layout locally (url_verifier gives a documented false-negative on this large PDF for multi-word tokens). Business Standard's Mar-2016 report of a live PNGRB tariff order on this exact pipeline is independent secondary confirmation that it is a real, in-service, regulated asset.
Listed in PNGRB's Natural Gas Pipeline (NGPL) register; trivially correct.

PNGRB's 2010 order authorises this as a common-carrier pipeline network under Regulation 17(1) of the PNGRB (Authorizing Entities to Lay, Build, Operate or Expand Natural Gas Pipelines) Regulations 2008 -- transmission-class common-carrier infrastructure, not CGD distribution.

OCR'd the original scanned PDF (no text layer; used pdftoppm + tesseract) since url_verifier can only confirm 200+token, not read image PDFs. Verbatim: '...the said pipeline project which has already been completed and commissioned between year 1991 to 2005...' -- this is PNGRB's own regulatory finding based on GAIL's submitted proof of commissioning, directly supporting StartYear1=1991 as the start of that range. Correctly NOT sourced from the 12.05.2010 authorisation date, which per the India playbook would be the wrong field to date it from -- this pipeline was built well before PNGRB existed and was authorised retroactively.

Confirmed to exact 2dp precision (16.00 MMSCMD authorised) in the Feb-2024 PNGRB register; matches (rounded) in the Jan-2016 (16.000) and May-2026 (16.0) editions. See the linked spec-history validity note: the 2010 authorisation order itself provisionally designated only 4.0 MMSCMD as 'common carrier capacity' pending final determination, while GAIL's indicated total network capacity was 15.997 MMSCMD (~16) -- every later register shows Authorised Capacity=16, i.e. the final determination landed at GAIL's originally-indicated total, not the 2010 provisional common-carrier subset. Single-origin (PNGRB) across three separately-dated editions -> tier medium rather than high, despite a decade of stability.

Exact match (877.86 km authorised) in the Feb-2024 PNGRB register; matches (rounded) in the Jan-2016 (877.9) and May-2026 (878) editions. Note: PNGRB's own operating-length column has since dipped slightly BELOW the authorised figure (864.90 km in 2024, 867 km in 2026) -- normal register noise, not evidence of a shortfall, since the row still sits in the 'OPERATIONAL' section with no under-construction length recorded. See the linked spec-history validity note re: this authorised length growing from 834.81 km at the original 2010 authorisation to 877.86-878 km by 2016 onward. Single-origin (PNGRB) across three editions -> tier medium.

PNGRB's tie-in-connectivity table lists several ONGC KG-basin fields (Madnam, Odalarevu/S1-VA, Bantumilli) feeding into 'GAIL's KG Basin Network' via named tie-in pipelines, confirming the network's gas is drawn from Krishna-Godavari basin fields. Caveat: the fuller title used in the 2016 PNGRB register is 'K.G. Basin network (+RLNG+RIL)', indicating the network also carries regasified LNG and Reliance Industries' (KG-D6) gas -- so 'Krishna Godavari Field' captures the dominant/geographically-defining source but the network is not exclusively fed by a single named field. Not proposing a change, noting for completeness.

PNGRB confirms Andhra Pradesh as a state the network passes through (also lists Puducherry -- see attribution caveat in validity). Not proposing Start*/End District fills: this is a multi-segment local network (2-18 inch diameter range across East Godavari, West Godavari, and Krishna districts per the original authorisation annexure), not a simple point-to-point line, so no single district value would be accurate for Start or End.

PNGRB lists GAIL as the sole authorised entity for this network across all three register editions checked (2016/2024/2026); Business Standard independently identifies it as 'the company's [GAIL's] K.G. Basin natural gas pipeline network' in unrelated financial reporting on a 2016 tariff order. Two independent origins confirming 100% GAIL ownership -> tier high.

summary: P0933 (KG Basin Gas Pipeline) is real, correctly classified as an operating GAIL common-carrier transmission network, and not a duplicate of any other roster row; every ref cluster staged as REFS_ADDED (tier high for Status/Owner via PNGRB+Business Standard+Times of India, tier medium for Capacity/Length/PipelineType/FuelSource/Location/Start via PNGRB's register -- single-origin but reconfirmed across three separately-dated editions plus an OCR'd primary 2010 authorization order). Two caveats staged, no UNRESOLVED: (1) the current 877.86 km / 16.00 MMSCMD figures supersede a documented, explained 2010 baseline (834.81 km / 4.0 MMSCMD provisional common-carrier capacity) -- not a sheet error; (2) PNGRB's register lists this network as also traversing Puducherry, which GEM's EndState/Province does not currently record -- flagged for Update, not changed here.
